newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker buys stake in Britain's McNulty.
newsitem.headline: Aker buys stake in Britain's McNulty.

text.p: Norway's Aker Oil and Gas Technology ASA has bought 70 percent of stock in McNulty Offshore Services to strengthen its position in Britain, especially in the floating production sector, Aker said in Tuesday.

Aker said in a statement that McNulty, a medium-size yard near Newcastle, northern England, fits out ships and semisubmersible platforms for oil production. It repairs rigs, carries out upgrades and builds modules of up to 4,000 tonnes.
Aker said it bought the shares for about 50 million crowns.

"Aker wants to strengthen its market position as a total supplier in the fields of operation, maintenance and modification by using competence in the existing organisation as well as in McNulty," the statement said.
"Aker regards the market in Britain as big and stable in the years to come, and demand for floating production platforms is considerable and growing," it said.
Aker Oil and Gas Technology is a subsidiary of offshore construction and building materials group Aker ASA.
